title: My AI kept buying the exact same failed breakout and I couldn't figure out why
author: CarQuirky5392
selftext:
I've been testing a model on AMD 5 minute candles and noticed it took basically the same bad long three mornings in one week. Around 10:00 AMD would push above the opening range, model confidence jumped over 0.70, then it would enter right before price came back inside.

Pulled up Monday's trade on moon.com and finally noticed volume was actually getting weaker on each push, something I wasn't feeding into the model at all. Added relative volume for the breakout candle and reran 14 months of data.

Trade count dropped from 286 to 219 and it removed 31 losing breakouts. Still not convinced the filter isn't just helping this particular sample, but at least I finally understand why those entries looked so stupid manually.

comments.author: OrderAgile6407
comments.body: Have you tried separating the first breakout attempt from the second/third? I wonder if relative volume is really identifying exhaustion after repeated attempts rather than weak breakouts generally

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
the "not convinced it isn't just this sample" instinct is the right one and most people skip straight past it. the check I'd do is look at which 31 breakouts it removed. if they cluster in a couple of months, or in one regime of AMD, the filter learned that stretch and not the behaviour. if they're spread across the 14 months roughly evenly it's probably real.

and the fact you found it by looking at a chart and going "oh, the volume" rather than by grid searching features is a point in its favour. filters with a story behind them survive longer than filters that came out of a search.

comments.author: Inevitable_Art7528
comments.body: 219 trades is still a decent sample but I’d definitely keep the next chunk completely out of sample. The fact that the filter makes intuitive sense helps but 14 months of AMD is still one stock in one particular market environment.

replies.author: DemonicAccomplice
replies.body: Yeah the single stock part is what I’m most suspicious of. AMD has had some pretty specific intraday behavior over that stretch, so 219 trades could still be teaching me more about AMD than about breakouts. I’m going to keep the next AMD block untouched and then run the exact same relative volume rule on NVDA without retuning it.

comments.author: Abject_Disaster7292
comments.body:
We ran into the same blind spot. Entries that looked clean on the chart but had no volume behind the move. The losses that hurt most were all in that bucket. Adding a relative volume check to breakout entries is on the list now partly because of exactly what you described.

What threshold did you land on for the rvol filter? Hard cutoff or weighted into confidence?
